key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves next-step CFD surrogate reconstruction by capturing both global flow patterns and localized multiscale structures.
engineering_relevance: This can speed up fluid simulation workflows for real-world benchmarks while preserving physically meaningful wake and interaction features.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding for multiscale flow representations
Physics-biased self-attention guided by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining via Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Evaluated on cylinder-wake flow and fluid-structure interaction benchmarks, the model achieved the best reported aggregate errors, including 0.05875 NRMSE and 0.97019 Pearson correlation on cylinder wake and 2.70×10^-4 NRMSE on FSI.
watch_item: Results come from specific benchmark settings, so generalization to other geometries, regimes, or rollout horizons may require additional validation.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
